questions.prompt: What does time to first token (TTFT) measure in the Claude docs?

options.text: The time it takes to produce the complete response text.
options.explanation: That is the total latency. TTFT stops at the first token, which is why it matters with streaming.

options.text: Time from sending the prompt to the first token.
options.explanation: Right. It matters most when you stream, since users start reading at that point.

options.text: The time your request first waits in your own job queue.
options.explanation: Your own queue is outside the model call. TTFT starts when the prompt is sent.

questions.prompt: Which prompt instruction controls length better, according to the Claude docs?

options.text: Answer in exactly 120 words, no more and no fewer.
options.explanation: Claude counts tokens, not words. The docs say an exact word count is not as effective.

options.text: Answer in no more than three short sentences.
options.explanation: Right. The docs say limits in paragraphs or sentences work better than a word count.

options.text: Set max_tokens to 50 and accept cut-off replies.
options.explanation: The docs call max_tokens a blunt tool. A reply can end mid-sentence, so it suits short answers only.

questions.prompt: What does Claude's fast mode speed up?

options.text: Time to first token, but not the speed of output.
options.explanation: It is the other way around. The gain is in output tokens per second.

options.text: Only the processing of very long input prompts.
options.explanation: The docs describe output speed as the benefit, up to 2.5x output tokens per second.

options.text: Output tokens per second, not first-token time.
options.explanation: Right. The docs say the benefits focus on output tokens per second, and it is the same model.
